archetypes.name: kv-threading
archetypes.rationale: Pruned-empty rounds silently stop as small-clean if any of the three run-step3-review.sh seams or the continuation precedence ordering is wrong — the plan names all seams explicitly but the reviewer should verify they exist in the current scripts and that allowlists cannot drop the new KVs.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan threads PANEL_PRUNED_EMPTY through three separate seams in run-step3-review.sh (the loop-stdout KV parse case, the inner-env read allowlist, and the result_env_kvs/phase_driver_write_result_env set), and the plan-review-continuation.sh pruned-empty branch must be placed after cap-reached and --approve checks but before the small-clean default elif chain. Verify that every named seam in the plan actually appears in the existing scripts in the scope file list, and that the placement precedence described matches how the continuation checks are currently ordered. Check whether any newly threaded KV (PRUNE_ROUND_NUM, PANEL_PRUNED_EMPTY) at any layer could be silently dropped by an allowlist, a case statement missing the new arm, or a source/kv_get call that only reads a hardcoded set of keys. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: label-attribution
archetypes.rationale: Over-pruning (Failure Mode 2) is entirely driven by whether the label normalization chain in the record subcommand matches what collect-findings.sh and aggregate-findings.sh currently produce — the plan references specific functions by name and the reviewer should verify they exist and output the assumed token shapes.
archetypes.prompt_body: The record subcommand's accepted_count attribution depends on exact normalized token equality using two distinct tokenization rules: pipe-split plus phase-suffix/trailing-parenthetical normalization for code-review reviewer_slots cells, and comma/whitespace split for plan-review finding_reviewers cells. Verify that the normalization functions referenced (phase2/phase3/retry suffix-strip loop from collect-findings.sh, one-trailing-parenthetical strip from aggregate-findings.sh) exist in those source files and produce the output shapes the plan assumes. Check that the harness fixtures described for test-reviewer-prune.sh use real manifest output basenames and assert shared-prefix non-collision (dyn-foo-output.txt must not match dyn-foo-codex-output.txt) as the plan specifies. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: degradation-denominator
archetypes.rationale: Multiple scripts compute thresholds from slot counts and all must switch to post-filter counts; any missed denominator target would produce false DEGRADED_ROUND=true on valid pruned runs, and the narrow fail-closed guard for dynamic-only panels introduces a new trigger condition that must be verified against the existing check-reviewer-failure-threshold.sh contract.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan replaces several hardcoded slot-count denominators with post-filter values: STATIC_SLOT_COUNT and DYNAMIC_SLOTS recomputation in dispatch-panel.sh, the floor-half degradation threshold and succeeded-paths comparison in dispatch-plan-review-panel.sh, and static_archetype_coverage_ok's expected archetype set in review-core.sh. Verify that each script in the scope file list that currently derives a threshold or coverage gate from a slot count is explicitly named in the plan as a denominator update target, and flag any path that computes such a value but is not listed. Check the narrow fail-closed guard for dynamic-only pruned panels in check-reviewer-failure-threshold.sh: confirm the opt-in flag name and the trigger condition (zero static rows in filtered manifest) are both specified in the plan and align with how that script currently structures its threshold logic. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
